    // The contact between a ball and an oriented box, found from the box point
    // nearest the ball's centre. When the centre is INSIDE the box that nearest
    // point IS the centre and carries no direction, so the fallback pushes the ball
    // out along the line of centres — not the true minimum-translation direction,
    // which would be through the nearest face. A solver fed centre-inside-box
    // contacts has already lost; the fallback exists so that one bad frame recovers
    // instead of producing a zero normal.
    Collide(a: Sphere, b: Box3D): Array<ContactPoint3D>
    {
        var nearest = b.ClosestPoint(a.Center);
        var d = a.Center.Between(nearest);
        var distance = d.Magnitude;
        var outward = b.Center.Between(a.Center);
        var fallback = outward.MagnitudeSquared > 0.0
            ? outward.Normalize.Negative
            : Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
        var normal = (distance > 0.0 ? d / distance : fallback).FromVectorUnchecked;
        var penetration = distance > 0.0 ? a.Radius - distance : a.Radius;
        return MaybeContact(penetration > 0.0, FreshContact(nearest, normal, penetration));
    }

    // The contact between a ball and a capsule, which is the ball-versus-ball test
    // run against the capsule's surface: a capsule is the set of points within its
    // radius of a segment, so the nearest capsule surface point already carries the
    // whole shape. A ball centre inside the capsule has no separating direction and
    // reports no contact rather than an arbitrary one.
    Collide(a: Sphere, b: Capsule3D): Array<ContactPoint3D>
    {
        var nearest = b.ClosestPoint(a.Center);
        var d = a.Center.Between(nearest);
        var distance = d.Magnitude;
        var penetration = a.Radius - distance;
        var normal = (distance > 0.0 ? d / distance : Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)).FromVectorUnchecked;
        return MaybeContact(distance > 0.0 && penetration > 0.0,
            FreshContact(nearest, normal, penetration));
    }

    // Corner `index` (0 to 7) of an oriented box: bit 0 selects the +X half, bit 1
    // the +Y half and bit 2 the +Z half, each along the box's own axes.
    BoxCorner(b: Box3D, index: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var f = b.Orientation.Basis3D;
        return b.Center
            + f.X * (b.Size.Width * (index % 2 == 1 ? 0.5 : -0.5))
            + f.Y * (b.Size.Height * ((index / 2) % 2 == 1 ? 0.5 : -0.5))
            + f.Z * (b.Size.Depth * (index / 4 == 1 ? 0.5 : -0.5));
    }

    // The contacts between an oriented box and an infinite plane: one point per box
    // CORNER that has crossed to the plane's negative side, so the manifold is four
    // points when the box lies flat, two when it rests on an edge, and one when it
    // balances on a corner. That is the whole reason a manifold is a SET of points
    // — a face contact solved through a single point cannot resist toppling, and
    // the box would rock forever.
    //
    // No clipping and no reduction: up to eight points, kept as found. Production
    // solvers reduce a manifold to four points to bound solver cost; which four are
    // kept changes which contacts are solved, so that reduction is a separate
    // decision and not a detail of this test.
    Collide(a: Box3D, b: Plane): Array<ContactPoint3D>
    {
        var normal = b.Normal.Vector.Negative.FromVectorUnchecked;
        return MapRange(8, i => BoxCorner(a, i)).FlatMap(corner =>
            MaybeContact(b.SignedDistance(corner) < 0.0,
                FreshContact(corner, normal, -b.SignedDistance(corner))));
    }

    //==
    // # Manifolds
    //
    // A manifold is a pair test's answer plus the two facts a pair test cannot
    // know: which bodies the shapes belong to, and what their materials combine to.
    // Keeping those out of the pair tests is what lets one
    // `Collide(Sphere, Plane)` serve a body pair, a trigger query and a law test.

    // The manifold for a body pair from points a pair test already produced, with
    // the pair's coefficients given directly. Normal is taken from the first point,
    // which every test in this file fills with the shared pair normal; an empty
    // manifold reports +Z, a value nothing reads because a manifold with no points
    // contributes no constraint rows.
    Manifold(bodyA: BodyIndex, bodyB: BodyIndex, points: Array<ContactPoint3D>,
        friction: Number, restitution: Proportion): ContactManifold3D
        => ContactManifold3D(
            bodyA,
            bodyB,
            points,
            points.Count > 0 ? points[0].Normal : Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0).FromVectorUnchecked,
            friction,
            restitution);

    // The manifold for a body pair whose two materials are merged into the pair's
    // coefficients. The overload above, taking the merged numbers, exists beside
    // this one because merging reads `MaterialCombine` — a sum type, and therefore
    // C#-only until the other backends emit sums (SEMANTICS.md, section 7). A
    // caller on a backend without sums combines its coefficients itself and uses
    // the other overload; nothing else in the contact pipeline touches a sum.
    Manifold(bodyA: BodyIndex, bodyB: BodyIndex, points: Array<ContactPoint3D>,
        materialA: PhysicsMaterial, materialB: PhysicsMaterial): ContactManifold3D
        => Manifold(bodyA, bodyB, points,
            CombinedFriction(materialA, materialB),
            CombinedRestitution(materialA, materialB));

    //==
    // # Constraint rows
    //
    // Flattening a manifold into rows is where the solver's per-iteration cost is
    // decided, so everything that is constant across iterations is computed exactly
    // once, here: the friction basis, and the separation speed restitution asks for.

    // The separation speed the solver should aim for along the normal, in meters
    // per second. `approachSpeed` is the CURRENT relative normal speed, negative
    // when the bodies are closing. A contact closing slower than the threshold is
    // treated as resting and asks for zero — without that cut-off a body sitting on
    // the floor buzzes forever, because gravity re-supplies exactly the approach
    // speed that restitution then hands back.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_restitution)
    RestitutionTarget(approachSpeed: Number, restitution: Proportion, threshold: Speed): Number
        => approachSpeed < -threshold.Amount
            ? -restitution.Value * approachSpeed
            : 0.0;

    // One manifold point as a solver row, with the friction basis and the
    // restitution target resolved. `approachSpeed` is the relative normal speed the
    // caller measured at the point before any solving.
    ConstraintRow(m: ContactManifold3D, p: ContactPoint3D, approachSpeed: Number,
        threshold: Speed): ContactConstraint3D
    {
        var tangent = Tangent(p.Normal);
        return ContactConstraint3D(
            m.BodyA,
            m.BodyB,
            p.Position,
            p.Normal,
            tangent,
            Bitangent(p.Normal, tangent),
            p.Penetration,
            m.Friction,
            m.Restitution,
            RestitutionTarget(approachSpeed, m.Restitution, threshold),
            p.NormalImpulse,
            Impulse.FromAmount(0.0),
            Impulse.FromAmount(0.0));
    }
